title: Income tax reassessment - the time limits after recent legal changes
p1:
Received an income tax reassessment notice after several years?

Many taxpayers assume the department can reopen any old return whenever it finds a possible issue. That is not always true.
p2: The law places clear time limits on reassessment proceedings. Recent changes have reduced uncertainty by creating different timelines depending on the value and nature of the income that may have escaped assessment.
p3:
In simple terms, a tax officer generally cannot go back indefinitely. For many cases, reassessment is restricted to a shorter period, while higher-value cases may allow a longer window if specific conditions are met.

The practical takeaway: receiving a notice does not automatically mean the demand is valid. Checking the assessment year, notice date, and applicable time limit is the first step before responding.
conclusion: Have you ever received an old income tax notice and wondered whether it was legally within the allowed time limit?
